meta.title: What are we called to carry—and what now requires a team?
meta.subtitle: A candid view of the ministry, the systems already built, the demands on Ryan and Brooke, and the decisions needed for the next 90 days.
meta.confidentialNote: Private working material prepared for Ryan Fox and Jon Perron. Please do not forward the page or access code.

sections.heading: The table is the ministry. The systems exist to support and multiply it.
sections.lede: USA Missionaries provides the covering. Kitchen Table Gospel is the frontline practice. DOS continues the relationship and makes multiplication visible. Operations supports the people, stewardship, and administration underneath it.

items: USA Missionaries — Covering: Recruit, equip, support, and connect missionaries across the United States.
Kitchen Table Gospel — Frontline practice: Disciple-making in homes, groups, coffee shops, and everyday relationships.
Discipleship Operating System — Continue & multiply: Help people act, grow, disciple others, and make aggregate fruit visible.
Operations — Support & steward: Onboarding, giving, finance, communication, compliance, and reporting.

blocks.title: Meeting outcome
blocks.text: Protect the core assignment, name what pauses, and identify the first responsibilities that must move off Ryan and Brooke.

sections.heading: This is no longer only vision or infrastructure.
sections.lede: Real relationships, referrals, groups, giving, and multiplication are already present. The question is how to steward the momentum without allowing the work to consume the people carrying it.

sections.heading: Not every good opportunity should receive the same kind of yes.
sections.lede: The portfolio needs clear categories so the core ministry remains protected while partnerships, paid work, and future ideas are handled deliberately.

blocks.caption: A working triage model for the meeting—not a final organizational decision.

items: Mission of Reconciliation / Fourth Quarter: More than freedom ministry: call seasoned believers into reconciliation, purposeful service, and discipling the next generation. Decide whether Fourth Quarter becomes a focused recruiting pathway inside DOS.
ZOE Church marriage ministry: A possible church partnership centered on training couples through apprenticeship at the table. Clarify scope, leaders, curriculum, timing, and ownership before launch.

Organization-specific DOS: River Valley Church and Engage Your Destiny illustrate how one operating system could be tailored to churches, veteran ministry, and para-ministry partners such as Mac Ministries.

SAVE Standard / The Lord's Army: Related but separate initiatives. Define Ryan's role, organizational boundaries, ownership, and time limits so each effort has a clear home and does not blur the core assignment.

blocks.title: Earned-revenue vision: Tent Maiker
blocks.text: An AI development company helping contractors, businesses, churches, and ministries build systems and organizational capacity without immediately hiring a full internal team. Viable first pilots: Chicken Coop Company · Come to Life Concrete. Initial proof of the model, followed by carefully scoped work with other contractors and ministry partners.

blocks.title: Fixed-duration contract: SHINE Founders Weekend
blocks.text: Brooke is contracted by SHINE to coordinate one event, October 1–4, 2026. It could lead to future event work, but there is no assumed ongoing commitment today. Current objective: Complete this event well, document the work, and establish a clean handoff afterward.

sections.heading: The opportunity is real. So is the capacity limit.
sections.lede: The immediate need is not more ideas. It is a truthful picture of what Ryan uniquely needs to lead, what can be delegated, and what the current financial position can responsibly support.

blocks.note: Cumulative giving, cash on hand, monthly support, and monthly need are different measures. No runway is stated until monthly organizational burn and household obligations are confirmed.

rows: Quiet time, marriage, five children, two long men's groups, individual discipleship, table ministry, couple training, fundraising, product review, operations, partnerships, and temporary commitments.
Ryan uniquely brings spiritual vision, frontline relationships, training, product direction, fundraising, and partner development. Routine execution cannot continue converging on him.
The organization has meaningful cash and giving momentum, but still faces a $4,879 monthly support gap. Hiring decisions require a verified burn rate and runway.
